projects.name: Casa Lumen
projects.summary: A house drawn around the horizon, resolved in section before a single material was chosen.
body: The site falls forty metres from the approach road to the water. Rather than terrace it, the house is set as two stone planes holding a shaded court between them, with the long axis ending at the sea and never at a wall.
Glass disappears between the planes. The entry compresses through stone and timber before the room opens in one controlled reveal, and the reverse journey reconstructs the threshold exactly.
Travertine is honed rather than polished throughout. Oak is quarter-sawn and brushed. Nothing was added to be noticed.
projects.heroAlt: Casa Lumen seen from the coastal approach

gallery.alt: The atrium opening toward the sea
The living room at the datum of the water

projects.name: Casa Vent
projects.summary: A cliff house that reads as one continuous section from the road to the rock.
body: The brief asked for four bedrooms on a plot that could reasonably hold two. The answer was to stop thinking in floors and draw the house as a single descending section, each room half a level below the last.
Circulation runs along the rock face, daylit from above, so the rooms themselves are free to face only the water.
The roof is a single folded plane. From the approach the house is a low wall; from the sea it is five storeys.
projects.heroAlt: Casa Vent above the water at dusk

projects.name: Casa Sal
projects.summary: A whitewashed fisherman's house reopened around a single shaft of light.
body: Nothing was added to the footprint. Four centuries of partitions were removed, one chimney was kept, and a light shaft was cut through three floors where the stair had been.
The new stair wraps that shaft in oak. Everything else is lime plaster, applied by hand and left unsealed so the walls continue to move with the weather.
The house now has fewer rooms than when we found it, and considerably more space.
projects.heroAlt: Casa Sal interior under the light shaft

projects.name: Casa Pedra
projects.summary: Two courts cut from the same stone language, one for water and one for shade.
body: The plot is flat, exposed and inland of the cliff path, so the house makes its own landscape. Two courts are cut into a single stone mass: one planted and shaded, one holding a shallow bathing pool.
Rooms are arranged as a loop around them, so there is no corridor in the house and no room without two aspects.
The external walls are close to blank. Everything the house has to offer is held inside.
projects.heroAlt: The bathing court at Casa Pedra

gallery.alt: The living loop around the planted court

projects.name: Casa Nord
projects.summary: A house and a working studio that share a wall and almost nothing else.
body: The client is a painter who wanted to stop commuting to work and did not want to live in a studio. The two programmes share one long wall and are otherwise deliberately separate: different entrances, different light, different ceiling heights.
The studio takes north light through a sawtooth roof. The house takes everything else.
The shared wall is the only place they meet, and it holds the kitchen on one side and the wash-up on the other.

gallery.alt: The shared wall from the house side
